name: Flockquake
mood: Velvet pressure fields fracture into lime, cobalt and coral stencil worlds.
credits: Glaze original artwork, built-in OpenAI image generation; original native widget geometry by lane B.
prompt: ONE original tall1290:2796 portrait wallpaper for Glaze FLOCKQUAKE. Photograph straight down of an astonishing physical electrostatic FLOCK PRINT on very pale lilac paper: hand-cut adhesive stencils hold DENSE SHORT VELVET FIBRES standing upright, crisp stencil edges with tiny loose flock particles, clearly visible directional pile, 0.5mm raised velour relief with tiny edge shadows, NOT fuzzy toys, fabric weaving, plush sculpture or digital gradient. In lower55% an invented tectonic storm-world of broad flattened angular cobalt plaques, acid-lime zigzag pressure ridges and three large coral-pink perforated cloud slabs interlock at impossible offsets; bold asymmetric stencilled silhouettes, strange square apertures, disconnected small tabs floating in pale lilac negative-space channels. Every colored region has unmistakably matte densely flocked velvet pile, the paper negative spaces are perfectly bare and smooth. Low grazing light makes fibre detail and subtle raised stencil outlines visible without dimensional objects. Palette acid lime #B5E247, saturated cobalt #343AB5, coral #F5838C, deep purple #291747, paper #E5DDF0. Upper45% mostly calm bare lilac paper for icons with only a sparse flock-dust trace along one edge; strongest forms at base and right. Experimental art-school craftprint, playful yet expertly controlled, no real objects, animals, faces, letters, text, numbers, logos, borders, mockup, UI, clock/time/date/battery/weather readings. One continuous crafted wallpaper, no contact sheet.
